goals.title: Carve a boat for all your friends
goals.critique: This is round 13's boat again, and the rework answers both of its named faults: a waterline and tilt drawn live on the hull while you cut turn blind sculpting into reading, and daily sea states plus loads that differ (canoe, barge, the boat for everyone) give a reason to carve more than one hull. The capsize as the last friend jumps in is still the strongest clip on the table, and the road starts with a film of three hulls from their own meshes, which is the right first proof. But carving a hull and watching it capsize is still familiar from ship sandboxes, and the new variety is a list of errands (race, barge, islands) rather than a deeper mechanic. Whether an adze stroke by mouse feels like shaping and not like slow erasing is still untested.

goals.title: Ride the hook you bent
goals.critique: This is the fourth round of the wire line. Fatigue that builds ride by ride and lines that differ answer last round's worry that the loop collapses into one line ridden again, and a hook that dulls where it is tired is a good thing to read. But the pitch is now two sentences and a paragraph of rules, it is wordier than last round, and fatigue that is visible yet still fails on the eleventh ride risks feeling like a hidden durability counter rather than something learned. The whole bet still rests on the unbuilt rod solver with plasticity and fatigue, and the filmed bend is the only step that exists after four rounds.

goals.title: Dam the stream
goals.critique: This one is new, and it is the plainest pitch so far: carry stones and clay, pile them across the stream, plug the leaks while the water climbs, and every minute has a clear job with the water answering at once. It sits squarely on the human's direction, with material gathered, carried and built into something whose load grows until it fails, and a full pond that changes the island (swimming, a mill) is a payoff that stays. But damming water and flooding a valley are well worn in god games, colony builders and sandboxes, so nobody will name this game after it. The promised moment happens in the night rain, while the player is likely not there, so the burst is watched, not caused. Shallow water over the heightfield is one of the more tractable physics bets here, but a wall that cracks from water pressure needs a structural model the road names and does not price.
